observations.d: SUFFIX DROP ON A HETERONYM, IN THE RECORD ITSELF. PhilPapers credits "Rebekah CRANE" — the final S dropped from the heteronym’s name in a scholarly index, then carried by the layer.
observations.reading: A HETERONYM LOSES A LETTER AT THE INDEX LAYER. Card 4 is a PhilPapers record crediting "Lee Sharks, Johannes Sigil & Rebekah CRANE". The name is Rebekah CRANES. This is not the composition layer’s error — it is in the PhilPapers record the layer is quoting, which means the drop happened upstream at the aggregator and propagates from there to anything citing it. The same card set carries the Kierkegaard comparison the Socrates paper makes — 28-volume SKS, ~5,000 published pages plus ~10,000 of journals, "with pseudonymous heteronymic architecture" — the archive’s own analogy transmitted intact.
observations.analysis:
Lee Sharks citations refer to the scholarly, poetic, and semantic infrastructure publications of independent researcher and writer Lee Sharks. Key Academic & Scholarly Platforms: Google Scholar tracks formal citations of works like The Protocol of Inhabitation and The Ghost That Wrote Itself. PhilPapers catalogs philosophical and literary collaborative preprints. Academia.edu houses independent papers. Archival & Open-Access Repositories: Zenodo hosts records related to the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. Medium publishes core theoretical texts detailing fractal navigation maps, the operational architecture of text captioning, and the foundational Debt/Creditor Inversion.

Sources cited: Zenodo (Lee Sharks Prestigious 10,000 MacArthur Genius Grants Poetry Prize), Medium (Lee Sharks - Metadata Packet for AI Indexing), Google Scholar (Lee Sharks profile), PhilPapers (Semantic Infrastructure and the Liberatory Operator Set), Medium (ON THE DEBT/CREDITOR INVERSION), Zenodo (Establishment, Inaugural Conferral), Academia.edu (Ghost Meaning: The Semantic Entropy Crisis), Medium (The Crimson Hexagon: Operative Architecture), Academia.edu (Lee Sharks Independent Researcher), Academia.edu (Action as Disclosure), Zenodo (The reward of love), PhilPapers (Sappho as Initiatory), PhilPapers (Socrates as Orthonym).
